in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

apprenticeship_location.description: The country where the child has started an apprenticeship, where relevant.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I'm asking about one child - my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! I'd like to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me start with some basic questions:

**How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Since Alex is 17, I need to understand his current situation as the rules are different for children over 16.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, staying in school, college, or an approved training course)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in school or college at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex is 17 and not in approved education or training, I need to ask:

**Has Alex recently left education or training (within the last 20 weeks) and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. I have a few more questions about Alex's current situation:

**Is Alex currently working, and if so, how many hours per week does he work?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One more important question:

**Is Alex claiming any benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Now I need to understand a bit about your own circumstances:

**Do you live in the UK, and does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Are you currently responsible for Alex - meaning you provide for his needs such as food, clothes, and accommodation?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am. I provide for all his needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One final question:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm sorry to inform you that **you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

While you normally qualify for Child Benefit for children under 16, **for children aged 16 or over** (up to age 20), they must be staying in approved education or training for you to continue receiving Child Benefit.

Since Alex is 17 and is not currently in approved education or training, he doesn't meet the eligibility criteria. Additionally, he hasn't recently left education to register with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services (which would allow Child Benefit to continue for up to 20 weeks).

Although you live in the UK, Alex lives with you, you're responsible for his upkeep, and he's not working or claiming benefits, these factors alone aren't sufficient once a child reaches 16 - the education or training requirement becomes critical at that age.

If Alex's circumstances change and he goes back into approved education or training, you may be able to claim Child Benefit at that point.
